_meta.indication: Indicated for symptomatic relief of non-infectious diarrhea in adult patients with HIV/AIDS on anti-retroviral therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (four weeks) and placebo-free (twenty weeks), multicenter study with a two-stage adaptive design; Stage 1 randomized 1:1:1:1 to crofelemer 125, 250, or 500 mg bid or placebo, Stage 2 randomized 1:1 to crofelemer 125 mg bid or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: HIV-positive patients on stable anti-retroviral therapy (ART) with a history of diarrhea for one month or more.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients with a clinical response, defined as ≤ 2 watery bowel movements per week during at least 2 of the 4 weeks of the placebo-controlled phase.
pivotal_trials.n: N=374 enrolled; in the double-blind period 136 received crofelemer 125 mg bid, 54 received 250 mg bid, 47 received 500 mg bid, and 138 received placebo.
pivotal_trials.result: A significantly larger proportion of patients in the crofelemer 125 mg bid group achieved clinical response vs placebo: 17.6% (24/136) vs 8.0% (11/138); treatment difference 9.6%; 1-sided p-value 0.0096.

nct_ctgov.title: Safety and Effectiveness of 3 Doses of Crofelemer Compared to Placebo in the Treatment of HIV Associated Diarrhea

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥ 3%) are upper respiratory tract infection, bronchitis, cough, flatulence and increased bilirubin; in the 125 mg bid group (N=229) vs placebo (N=274): upper respiratory tract infection 5.7% vs 1.5%, bronchitis 3.9% vs 0, cough 3.5% vs 1.1%.
target_moa: Crofelemer is an inhibitor of both the cAMP-stimulated CFTR chloride ion channel and the calcium-activated chloride channels (CaCC) at the luminal membrane of enterocytes, which regulate chloride and fluid secretion by intestinal epithelial cells; it acts by blocking chloride secretion and accompanying water loss.
modality: Other — oral botanical drug substance (oligomeric proanthocyanidin mixture derived from the red latex of Croton lechleri).

rems.type: DRISK reviewer concluded a REMS is not necessary to ensure the benefits of crofelemer outweigh the risks; labeling adequately addresses the safety risks.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was conducted for crofelemer.

summary.text: Fulyzaq (crofelemer), an oral botanical drug substance, received a priority NDA review and was approved on a full (non-accelerated) basis on December 31, 2012 for symptomatic relief of non-infectious diarrhea in adults with HIV/AIDS on anti-retroviral therapy, based on the pivotal ADVENT (NP303-101) trial; no advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required.

SUBJECT: Approval Action
TO: NDA 202292 Fulyzaq (crofelemer) delayed-release tablets

This new drug application provides for the use of Fulyzaq (crofelemer) delayed-release tablets for the symptomatic relief of non-infectious diarrhea in adult patients with HIV/AIDS on anti-retroviral therapy.
